video_title: Jayson Tatum’s MVP Case, the Clippers’ Lost Decade & NBA Surprise Teams | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's boxing debut and his professional development
quotes.excerpt: I love what Jaylen is doing nowadays. Low key in 20 years, you look back on his career, you're going to be like, 'Did you hoop or were you a superhero?'
quotes.quote: I love what Jaylen is doing nowadays. Low key in 20 years, you look back on his career, you're going to be like, 'Did you hoop or were you a superhero?' Shout out to him, shout out to him pushing the fold. I know he gets a lot of slack, but he's living his truth. The dude is down there like Iron Man, he's worth like 600 million, he's doing absolutely whatever he wants, and he looks prime and prepped. His body looks great.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' front office failures and the Kawhi Leonard deal
quotes.excerpt: This played out like a legal prosecution where the NBA cut deals. They cut a deal with Lawrence Frank, who only got six months.
quotes.quote: This played out like a legal prosecution where the NBA cut deals. They cut a deal with Lawrence Frank, who only got six months. They cut a deal obviously with Kawhi Leonard, who was at the center of all this. The only thing that Kawhi Leonard loses here is 700,000 dollars, which is a proverbial slap on the wrist for a guy that reportedly made in the neighborhood of 50 million dollars as a result of these side deals. Now, at some point, he's going to get to go on to Toronto, the Raptors are going to extend him, so he's not going to miss that 700,000 bucks. It strains credulity to believe that Kawhi didn't know what was going on behind the scenes.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' disastrous trade history and loss of draft assets
quotes.excerpt: This was the worst transaction for them in NBA history. This was the Exxon Valdez of transactions.
quotes.quote: This was the worst transaction for them in NBA history. This was the Exxon Valdez of transactions. This was the Titanic of transactions. The AOL Time Warner merger of transactions. This was catastrophic. I believe the final tally was 10 first-round draft picks, a couple of swaps and, oh yeah, the two-time MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. So nothing positive came out of this.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's expected scoring output for the upcoming season
quotes.excerpt: I think for sure personally, I think he's going to average about 30 a game.
quotes.quote: I think for sure personally, I think he's going to average about 30 a game. I think he's been waiting for these type of moments. Not to get rid of Jaylen Brown, but I think for eight or nine years of just always having to over here being like, 'No, he's got a loaded team, he can't be MVP this year, he can't do this this year.' I think sitting back, watching the game, getting smarter, but also seeing what Jaylen Brown was able to do with that team and being like, 'You know what, bro, when I come back, these guys are going to be prime, I'm going to be able to do a lot more.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of Mitchell Robinson on the Celtics' defense
quotes.excerpt: I love the addition of Mitchell Robinson. I'm not sure how many games you're going to get out of him.
quotes.quote: I love the addition of Mitchell Robinson. I'm not sure how many games you're going to get out of him, but I'm telling you, when I talk to people in Boston, Mitchell Robinson is a Joe Mazzulla guy. That's the kind of guy he wants. A guy that's going to go out there, gobble up rebounds, protect the paint, do all the things that Neemias Queta couldn't do last year, at least not in the right situations against the right types of matchups.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Derrick White's performance and need for improved shooting
quotes.excerpt: He did shoot sub-40 percent from the floor and from three-point range and that's got to get better.
quotes.quote: He did shoot sub-40 percent from the floor and from three-point range and that's got to get better. I think I hope that at 32 years old, he's still able to bring the same kind of defensive intensity that he can still be the playmaker that he was last season, but I need him to make shots. I need him to make shots and I'm a little worried that the slide we saw last year from Derrick White was not an aberration, but maybe a sign of things to come.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Pacers' roster moves and potential for a playoff run
quotes.excerpt: The Pacers just kind of punted on last season, made some moves, traded for a Ivica Zubac.
quotes.quote: The Pacers just kind of punted on last season, made some moves, traded for a Ivica Zubac, get Tyrese Haliburton back after the torn Achilles during the 2025 NBA Finals. And I think there are people out there wondering if they can pick up right where they left off. They were a playoff team in 2025 and went on one of the most improbable runs straight through the Eastern Conference playoffs into the NBA Finals.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The competitiveness of the Eastern Conference and Pacers' outlook
quotes.excerpt: The East is tough. The East is very, very tough. It's not what it was a couple years ago.
quotes.quote: The East is tough. The East is very, very tough. It's not what it was a couple years ago. I love Indiana, I love Coach Rick Carlisle, I love the fan base. I think their run was unbelievable, but if the Knicks weren't the Knicks, we wouldn't be talking about this. If the Knicks closed out and finished their breakfast, I don't think we'd be talking about this.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Magic's potential and roster talent
quotes.excerpt: I've been pretty bullish on the Orlando Magic for most of the summer.
quotes.quote: I've been pretty bullish on the Orlando Magic for most of the summer. I know, I keep it's like Charlie Brown and Lucy, like I keep trying to kick the football and it keeps getting taken away from me. Like the Magic have real talent. Like Paolo Banchero is an All-Star. Franz Wagner is an All-Star. Wendell Carter Jr. is a good big. Jalen Suggs is a good guard. Desmond Bane wasn't the missing piece last year, but maybe he still can be. Like I I think they have the talent to be a lot better than they were last year.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The role of Wendell Carter Jr. in the Magic's offense
quotes.excerpt: How does Zubac fit in to how they want to play? Because Zubac is a really good player.
quotes.quote: How does Zubac fit in to how they want to play? Because Zubac is a really good player. One of the top defensive centers in the NBA. He's not Miles Turner though. He's not Miles Turner. He's not Miles Turner. He does not play the way Miles Turner plays. Like Zubac is an inside the three-point line big man. And can I see him plug and play into the same spots Miles Turner was? No, I can't see that. Can I see him running pick and roll or pick and pop as effectively as Miles Turner did? No, I can't see that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Magic's need for a new offensive system
quotes.excerpt: They're going to have to work some magic again for this to work in Indy.
quotes.quote: They're going to have to work some magic again for this to work in Indy. He's going to have to come up with kind of a I don't want to say a new system because you don't want to it's not broken out there. You don't want to change too much because you got a lot of the same guys, you want to keep, you know, running things through Franz Wagner, keep running things through Paolo Banchero, keep doing what made you successful two years ago, but they got to figure out something new to do with Wendell Carter Jr. offensively because I think they're going to miss what Miles Turner brought to them on that end of the floor.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Wendell Carter Jr.'s effort and role on the team
quotes.excerpt: His reputation, he's always trying to make it work. Like you know what I mean? Even this being in the paint.
quotes.quote: His reputation, he's always trying to make it work. Like you know what I mean? Even this being in the paint is kind of hypothetical to the sense of just being like, 'I'm just here to help.' Like you know what I mean? He always try to tries to make himself available around the rim. He's always trying to fight for offensive rebounds. He's screening, he's doing his job, and I believe like of course, Indiana knows where a big man shooter away, but I think up until maybe the front office makes something happen, I don't even know if their shooters out there yet.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Clingan's development and defensive potential
quotes.excerpt: I think people don't comprehend how well he's been developing. He's one of the best offensive rebounders in the entire league.
quotes.quote: I think people don't comprehend how well he's been developing. He's one of the best offensive rebounders in the entire league. I think he takes great joy in defending that paint and anchoring that paint. And he's become a better picking pop shooter too, three or four threes per game to Mani Kamara. He's become a better shooter, he's locking shit down, 1,000 percent.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jrue Holiday's impact and the Trail Blazers' team dynamics
quotes.excerpt: And then the living legend, the the one and only, my goat, my hero, Jrue Holiday.
quotes.quote: And then the living legend, the the one and only, my goat, my hero, Jrue Holiday. He's going to make intangibles occur, bro, and when you put that in with Damian Lillard, who's saying, 'I didn't come here to waste my time,' I've watched his man carry me and the homies to Steam Room Mafia to 50 something wins, and we had no business doing that. I believe with that right type of mentality, but also too, to be able to have defenders and have all-around playmakers together, and they've already done some amazing things last year as well.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Trail Blazers' roster and potential for success
quotes.excerpt: They've got most of the band back together. You look at the starting lineup, they've got Andrew Nembhard.
quotes.quote: They've got most of the band back together. You look at the starting lineup, they've got Andrew Nembhard, they've got Aaron Nesmith, they've got Pascal Siakam, TJ McConnell coming off the bench. I like the Kelly Oubre Jr. signing. I think that's going to help them, versatile guy, plays multiple positions, has played some winning basketball over the years.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Ja Morant's struggles and potential for a turnaround
quotes.excerpt: Maybe the change of scenery for Ja Morant will lead to a revival.
quotes.quote: Maybe the change of scenery for Ja Morant will lead to a revival. It certainly needs to for him to have a future in the NBA. But all we know about Ja Morant right now, as we record this, is that he can't shoot, he's got a bum wheel, and he doesn't really defend. So, like, those are three things that are facts right now about Ja Morant. Not not conjecture, those are facts about Ja Morant.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Ja Morant's potential for a comeback and team fit
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to give an extra year to see what type of dog is in that fight because...
quotes.quote: I'm going to give an extra year to see what type of dog is in that fight because to have a body like Ja Morant, like I'm I'm or even like when you meet shooters who in practice go 98 for 100, I'm like, 'Hey, what in the rim, baby, like it was what was wrong with you mentally?' You know what I mean? And that's where I kind of want to see because we all had him as a big dog coming in last year and he really has to bounce back and it's a coach's lead to set the culture, but it's also a player's lead to lead and I wonder if his back is big enough, you know?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Avdija's contract and usage rate
quotes.excerpt: Danny Avdija's usage rate was 31 last year. That was a career high by a country mile.
quotes.quote: Danny Avdija's usage rate was 31 last year. That was a career high by a country mile. Like now he's coming back into a situation where Dame's going to have the ball, Ja's going to have the ball. Like how is Danny Avdija, who I don't know what his contract situation is, but he's got to be looking to get paid at some point, right? He like he wants, I'm sure he's going to want a new deal at some point. I forget what what his contract thing is like, but but he's going to have to sacrifice shots.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of having a 6-8 versatile player
quotes.excerpt: When you're a coach and this is a league, you hope you have a 6-8 do-it-all player.
quotes.quote: When you're a coach and this is a league, you hope you have a 6-8 do-it-all player. Like you know what I mean? Like when I walk into the locker room, if I was a coach, I'd be like, 'All right, we got Danny Avdija.' Or to sit here, we arguably have one of the best clutch players. Okay, how will the game start? How's the last five minutes of the game going to be played? So when you sit there, you're kind of looking and being like, 'Hey, the last five minutes, and we're coming down and Danny's older and you know, if Danny's on the floor, the geometry of the floor is going to be out to 35 feet.' You're trying to figure out like, 'Hey, when it comes down to my kill moments, you're going to give it to Danny for sure, but you're going to have to have the ball a lot of times in Danny Avdija's hand.'

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Avdija's contract situation and future
quotes.excerpt: Danny again, will be really interesting because he's making, I think around 12 million dollars this year.
quotes.quote: Danny again, will be really interesting because he's making, I think around 12 million dollars this year. He's got a contract next season for around 13 million dollars. That is a bargain for the Trail Blazers. But because of the way that the cap is set up and the rules are set up, he can't get an extension from the Blazers unless they have cap space to extend him. And they don't. They they've given up a lot of their caps with the sacrifice that Ja Morant's under contract for two more seasons at big numbers. Now, Dame is under a much more manageable contract, that's true. Um, but they're I think they might be in a tough spot with Danny because Danny's going to be looking around going, 'I I got to get my contract. I got to get my max dollars when my deal comes up in a couple of years.'
